runs.content: Visa (V) picked up at the previous close ($378.40) — entered on the financials sector's breakout to fresh all-time highs (XLF), a rally explicitly framed as capital rotating away from chip/AI-hyperscaler names, reinforced by Visa's own record high, a fiscal Q3 beat (+14% revenue, +10% payments volume) and Bill Ackman's disclosed ~$1.1B stake. RIVN was exited discretionarily (−9.14%, −$91) to keep the book at 35 open positions after V's entry — no mechanical stop-losses or T1/T2 triggers on the other 33 continuing positions; CMCL closed to within $0.39 of its T2 target. Portfolio net P&L: +$2,610 (+4.75% on $55,000).

Medtronic (MDT) picked up at the previous close ($92.04) — a clean Q1 FY2027 beat-and-raise (EPS $1.45 vs $1.39 est., revenue $9.8B vs $9.55B est., +13.7% YoY, broad-based across Cardiovascular +18.9%/Electrophysiology +29.1%) with a raised full-year guide on both revenue and EPS and only a modest ~3% stock reaction, chosen over today's bigger earnings movers Dell (Burry AI-capex conflict) and GitLab (already up 20%+, disqualified by strategy D's own rule). HPQ hit T1 @ $31.32 (+25.23%), banking ~$417 on the first tranche. ROK was exited discretionarily (−9.66%, −$97) to keep the book at 35 open positions after MDT's entry — no mechanical stop-losses or signal exits on the other 33 continuing positions. Portfolio net P&L: +$2,445 (+4.53% on $54,000).
